name: Udaipur
tagline: The city of lakes
description: Whitewashed palaces rise from Lake Pichola, rooftop cafés glow at sunset, and narrow lanes hide miniature-painting studios. Udaipur is Rajasthan at its most romantic and unhurried.

name: Jaipur
tagline: The pink city
description: Terracotta façades, hilltop forts and bazaars piled with block-printed cotton. Jaipur is bold, busy and deeply rewarding for heritage lovers.

name: Munnar
tagline: Tea hills in the clouds
description: Rolling emerald tea estates, misty mornings and waterfalls in the Western Ghats. Munnar is where you slow down with a cup of something freshly plucked.

name: Cairo
tagline: A thousand minarets
description: Fatimid gates, Coptic churches and the roar of a megacity on the Nile. Start with Khan el-Khalili and the Egyptian Museum, end with koshari at midnight.

name: Giza
tagline: Where the pyramids stand
description: The last surviving wonder of the ancient world sits at the edge of the city. Come early for quiet sand and soft light on the Great Pyramid and the Sphinx.

name: Luxor
tagline: The world's greatest open-air museum
description: Karnak's forest of columns on the east bank, royal tombs on the west, and hot-air balloons drifting over both at dawn.

name: Wayanad
tagline: Forested plateau of caves, peaks and waterfalls.
description: Wayanad is a green plateau district bordering Karnataka and Tamil Nadu, known for prehistoric cave carvings, spice plantations, wildlife sanctuaries and some of Kerala's best treks.

name: Thiruvananthapuram
tagline: Kerala's capital — beaches, museums and the Ponmudi hills.
description: The state capital combines colonial-era museums and temples with a coastline that stretches from Kovalam to the red cliffs of Varkala (Varkala municipality, in the north of the district). The hill station of Ponmudi is a short drive inland.

name: Kochi
tagline: Spice-trade port with layered colonial history.
description: Kochi's Fort Kochi and Mattancherry neighbourhoods are a walkable mix of Chinese fishing nets, Portuguese and Dutch buildings, Jewish heritage, art cafés and some of Kerala's best food.

name: Alappuzha
tagline: Houseboats drifting through palm-lined backwaters.
description: Alappuzha (Alleppey) is the gateway to Kerala's backwaters — a web of canals, lakes and paddy fields best explored by houseboat or village canoe.

name: Ooty
tagline: Queen of the Nilgiris — lakes, gardens and a toy train.
description: Udhagamandalam (Ooty) is a classic colonial-era hill station in the Nilgiri hills, famous for its botanical gardens, lake and the UNESCO-listed Nilgiri Mountain Railway.

name: Kodaikanal
tagline: Princess of hill stations, around a star-shaped lake.
description: Kodaikanal in the Palani hills is built around a man-made star-shaped lake, with pine forests, cliffs and walking paths.

name: Rameswaram
tagline: Island temple town on the edge of the Palk Strait.
description: Rameswaram is a major pilgrimage town on Pamban Island, known for the Ramanathaswamy Temple's corridors, the Pamban bridges and the abandoned town of Dhanushkodi.

name: Mahabalipuram
tagline: Pallava-era rock-cut monuments by the sea.
description: Mamallapuram (Mahabalipuram) is a UNESCO World Heritage site with 7th–8th century rock-cut temples, monolithic rathas and bas-reliefs on the Coromandel coast.

name: Coorg
tagline: Coffee estates, misty hills and Kodava culture.
description: Kodagu (Coorg) is a hilly district famous for its coffee and spice plantations, waterfalls, Tibetan settlements and distinctive Kodava cuisine.

name: Mysuru
tagline: City of palaces, silk and sandalwood.
description: Mysuru, the former seat of the Wodeyar dynasty, is known for the illuminated Mysore Palace, the Dasara festival, Chamundi Hill and its sweets.

name: Hampi
tagline: Boulder-strewn ruins of the Vijayanagara empire.
description: Hampi is a UNESCO World Heritage site spread across a surreal boulder landscape on the Tungabhadra river, with temples, bazaars and royal enclosures from the 14th–16th centuries.

name: Chikmagalur
tagline: Birthplace of Indian coffee and Karnataka's highest peak.
description: Chikkamagaluru is coffee country in the Baba Budangiri range, home to Mullayanagiri — Karnataka's highest peak — and many waterfalls.

name: Goa
tagline: Sun, sand and Indo-Portuguese heritage.
description: India's smallest state is known for its beaches, whitewashed churches, spice farms, laid-back villages and fiery seafood curries.

name: Manali
tagline: Gateway to the high Himalaya.
description: Manali sits at the head of the Kullu valley on the Beas river — a base for snow trips, adventure sports and road journeys towards Lahaul and Ladakh.

name: Leh-Ladakh
tagline: High-altitude lakes, passes and monasteries.
description: Leh is the base for exploring Ladakh's Buddhist monasteries, high passes and lakes like Pangong Tso. Allow time to acclimatise to the altitude (about 3,500 m).

name: Rishikesh
tagline: Yoga capital on the Ganga.
description: Rishikesh is a spiritual town in the Himalayan foothills, known for its suspension bridges, ashrams, the evening Ganga aarti and white-water rafting.

name: Lonavala
tagline: Monsoon getaway in the Sahyadri hills.
description: Lonavala and Khandala are hill towns between Mumbai and Pune, loved for monsoon waterfalls, forts and caves.

name: Kutch
tagline: The white salt desert and living crafts.
description: The Great Rann of Kutch is a vast seasonal salt marsh that turns into a white desert in winter, surrounded by craft villages.

name: Darjeeling
tagline: Tea gardens facing Kanchenjunga.
description: Darjeeling is a Himalayan hill town known for its tea, the Darjeeling Himalayan Railway and views of Kanchenjunga.

name: Kyoto
tagline: Temples, shrines and seasonal gardens.
description: Kyoto was Japan's capital for over a thousand years and keeps hundreds of temples, shrines, traditional streets and gardens.

name: Ubud
tagline: Bali's cultural heart among rice terraces.
description: Ubud is a town in Bali's uplands known for rice terraces, temples, crafts, yoga and traditional dance.
